 1                   I.    INTRODUCTION AND QUALIFICATIONS

 2   Q1.   PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 3   A.    My name is Steven A. Sierra. My business address is 100 N. Stanton Street,

 4         El Paso, Texas 79901.

 5

 6   Q2.   BY WHOM ARE YOU EMPLOYED AND IN WHAT CAPACITY?

 7   A.    I am employed by El Paso Electric Company ("EPE" or the "Company") as Director

 8         of Financial Accounting.

 9

10   Q3.   PLEASE SUMMARIZE YOUR EDUCATIONAL BACKGROUND AND

11         PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE.

12   A.    I graduated from The University of Texas at El Paso with a Bachelor of Business

13         Administration in Accounting, and a Master of Accountancy. I am a Certified

14         Public Accountant in the State of Texas and a member of the Texas Society of

15         Certified Public Accountants and the American Institute of Certified Public

16         Accountants. In addition, I received a graduate certificate from New Mexico State

17         University in Public Utility Regulation & Economics and have attended

18         professional development seminars sponsored by the American Gas Association

19         and Edison Electric Institute.

20                Upon graduation, I was employed in El Paso as a staff accountant at Desert

21         View Homes from 2010-2011, and at Hunt Companies, Inc. from 2011-2012, where

                                                  1
                                            Amended Filing
                                  EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY

                                       STEVEN A. SIERRA

 1         my primary responsibilities included the preparation of internal financial

 2         statements. I joined El Paso Electric Company in 2012 and have held various

 3         positions in the Energy Accounting, Financial Accounting and Financial Planning

4          & Analysis departments. My responsibilities in the various roles at EPE have

5          included the preparation and analysis of internal and external financial statements,

6          the preparation of financial statements for the Company's benefit plans and

7          overseeing the Company's annual budget and forecasting processes. In March

8          2022, I accepted my current position of Director-Financial Accounting.

9

10   Q4.   WHAT ARE YOUR PRINCIPAL AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY?

11   A.    I serve under the general direction of the Vice President-Controller and I oversee

12         the Company's financial accounting and financial reporting departments. I support

13         the establishment and maintenance of the Company's accounting principles,

14         practices, and procedures for the maintenance of its fiscal records and the

15         preparation of its financial reports.

16

17   Q5.   HAVE       YOU       PREVIOUSLY             TESTIFIED     BEFORE         UTILITY

18         REGULATORY BODIES?

19   A.    Yes. I have testified before the Public Utility Commission of Texas ("PUCT").

20

 1                           II.     PURPOSE OF TESTIMONY

 2   Q6.   WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR DIRECT TESTIMONY?

 3   A.    The purpose of my direct testimony is to summarize EPE's cost of service and

 4         revenue requirements, explain the New Mexico revenue deficiency, and specify the

 5         requested New Mexico rate increase.

 6                I also describe the Test Year Period cost of service adjustments to Base

 7         Period amounts reflected in this proceeding. Each of these adjustments is described

 8         later in my direct testimony and is supported by the various EPE witnesses as

 9         indicated below, including those adjustments which I specifically sponsor. A

10         complete listing of all Test Year Period adjustments to Base Period amounts is

11         included in Schedule A-3 and its related workpapers, and in Exhibit SAS-1. Each

12         of these adjustments is appropriate and reasonable and calculated in compliance

13         with Rule 17.9.530 of the New Mexico Administrative Code ("Rule 530").

14                Further, my testimony demonstrates that the Test Year Period costs for

15         employee compensation and benefits requested in this case are consistent with a

16         recent market study, are in compliance with recent New Mexico Public Regulation

17         Commission ("NMPRC" or "Commission") orders, and are just and reasonable,

18         including a rate base adjustment for EPE’s pension and OPEB plans.

19                Last, I support the reasonableness of Administrative and General ("A&G")

20         expenses and summarize the Rule 530 Schedules that I sponsor or co-sponsor.

21

8    Q14. WHEN WERE BASE RATES LAST ESTABLISHED FOR EPE?

9    A.   EPE's current base rates were established by the Commission in Docket No. 20-

10        00104-UT ("2020 Rate Case") using a Historical Test Year Period ending

11        December 31, 2019. Since the 2020 Rate Case, EPE's rate base and operating costs

12        have changed.

13

15        COST OF SERVICE EXPENSES YOU REFERENCED ABOVE?

17        Novela, since the 2020 Rate Case, EPE has incurred $2.4 billion (New Mexico

18        jurisdictional amount of $408.4 million) in construction expenditures to maintain

19        its local generating units and to maintain the Palo Verde Generating Station

20        ("PVGS"), as well as other general and intangible plant additions. EPE has also

21        made improvements in its transmission and distribution system to serve load

 5        testimonies, and EPE witness Prieto discusses EPE’s general and intangible plant

 6        additions in her direct testimony.

 7               Since the 2020 Rate Case, the Company has also experienced increases in

 8        operation and maintenance ("O&M") expenses to operate its PVGS and local

 2   Q17. WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF THIS SECTION OF YOUR TESTIMONY?

 4        adjustments to the cost of service. EPE witness Prieto sponsors the Company's rate

 5        base and describes the adjustments to rate base in her direct testimony, including

 8   Q18. WHAT SORTS OF ADJUSTMENTS TO BASE PERIOD DATA IS

 9        AUTHORIZED BY RULE 530 AND WHAT COMPANY SCHEDULE LISTS

10        THESE ADJUSTMENTS?

11   A.   According to Rule 530, an "Adjustment" is a calculation made with reasonable

12        accuracy to the book balance of accounts to reflect an annualization, a known and

13        measurable change, or an estimate based on projection for the full twelve-month

14        period of the Test Year Period. The Company's Test Year Period adjustments on

15        Schedule A-3 encompasses "Adjustments" under Rule 530.

16

17   Q19. WHAT ADJUSTMENTS DID EPE MAKE TO THE BASE PERIOD TO

18        DEVELOP THE TEST YEAR PERIOD?

19   A.   EPE made numerous adjustments to the total Company Base Period book balance

20        amounts to arrive at the Test Year Period amounts. The adjustments include

21        annualizations and known and measurable changes to O&M expenses and plant in

5         service adjustments in numerical order in my testimony. See Workpaper A-3 for

 6        backup and calculations for each adjustment to the Base Period. EPE witness

 7        Hernandez addresses allocation to the New Mexico jurisdiction, including direct

 8        assignment to a jurisdiction if appropriate, which enables the proper allocation of the

 9        adjustments to the New Mexico jurisdiction.

18                The resulting adjusted revenues and expenses are those that, if used as the

19        basis for setting rates for the prospective period following the ordering of final rates

20        in effect, will give the Company a reasonable opportunity to recover its reasonable

21        and necessary expenses.
